dystrophin‐null muscle has an increase in collagen cross‐link formation and that this is a key contributor to the increase in ECM stiffness.
dystrophin deficiency is associated with increased cross‐linking of collagen I, collagen VI, and collagen IV in skeletal muscle.

increased collagen cross‐link‐ing is a signature feature of dystrophin deficiency in murine, canine and human muscle, and is associated with increased ECM stiffness and altered muscle fiber structure.

the following aspects of collagen cross-linking: (i) the effect of dystrophin deficiency on collagen cross‐link formation, (ii) the role of the dystrophin‐glycoprotein complex (DGC) in regulating collagen cross‐link maturation, and (iii) the effect of collagen cross‐links on the biomechanical properties of dystrophic muscle.
